acceptance_criteria: A transition-matrix fixture proves active decision labels and status agree, legitimate close passes and unblocks, reopen is restored to decision before autonomous use, claim or arbitrary status drift is detected, and ordinary work cannot carry decision status without both labels. The validator runs in repository-owned pre-commit and CI gates. br ready, scheduler, and .beads/agent-plan.sh expose no owner decision and agree on actionable IDs. Documentation states that actor metadata is not authentication and raw bv robot planning is advisory.

title: Implement the checked autonomous plan wrapper and Viewer quarantine
description:
Close the implementation gap between the cooperative Beads policy and the agent workflow. The current validator detects invalid decision state, but raw Viewer robot planning can still recommend a status=decision issue and documentation alone cannot prevent an autonomous agent from claiming it. Implement a small checked repository wrapper that fails closed, compares the canonical br ready/scheduler result with tracked issue status and labels, and refuses to consume untrusted raw Viewer planning. Keep actor metadata cooperative; do not claim owner authentication. Make the wrapper useful to both humans and agents and keep it independent of Omnirepo product authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Keep the wrapper small and fail-closed. It is a repository workflow adapter over br and tracked JSONL, not a replacement tracker or a Viewer fork. It must be deterministic under stale/missing data and produce evidence that the test suite can compare.
acceptance_criteria: A tracked wrapper is the only autonomous planning entry point. It derives candidates from br ready and the configured scheduler, validates status and decision labels against tracked JSONL, excludes every decision and deferred/container issue, emits stable issue IDs plus blocker/reason evidence, and exits nonzero on disagreement or stale data. Raw bv robot-plan is explicitly advisory and cannot be used for claims. Fixtures cover active, closed, reopened, relabeled, blocked, deferred, and normal work; CI and pre-commit run the wrapper and a decision can never reach a claimable recommendation.
notes: Future self: a false-positive actionable decision is a safety failure. Prefer refusing to plan over silently trusting a disagreement.

title: Converge Omnirepo on its Constitution
description:
## Goal

Bring the current 0.8.x implementation into complete alignment with the ratified Omnirepo Constitution and routed Canon architecture.

## Current state

The quality baseline passes, but the product still exposes general repository creation, tag cloning, arbitrary shell execution, and ad hoc synchronization authority. It lacks canonical machine/source/repository configuration, source materialization, exact partials, contained atomic file transactions, verified scoped Git delivery, crash-recoverable durable accounting, bounded repair, and lawful release handling.

## Program rule

Decision-needed children are owner blockers and may not be guessed. Implementation preserves exact one-way authority, visible whole/section edges, independent outcomes, complete durable accounting, bounded sync-induced repair, and the constitutional limits. Actionable migration guidance is mandatory for breaking releases; an automated migrator is implemented only under its explicit decision.

## Success Criteria

See structured acceptance criteria; every mandatory child must close before the epic is eligible.
design: The delivery architecture is artifact-first and vertically sliced: owner decisions -> canonical machine authority -> immutable source snapshots/catalog -> explicit repository policy -> pure per-repository plans -> contained exact whole/partial transactions -> frozen repository/delta state -> configured verification -> operation-scoped local commit -> exact remote push -> one-repository initial pass -> bounded fleet fan-out -> separately invoked bounded repair -> durable final summary -> one public CLI. Legacy general orchestration is removed before replacement. Each outcome container is deferred while its leaf tasks are executed; after leaves close, reopen the container, verify its parent acceptance contract, and close it.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; the final implementation passes the Constitution gate across the full product surface; Cargo quality, MSRV, coverage, and pre-commit gates pass; public docs describe only the constitutional product.
notes: Autonomous agents claim leaf tasks from br ready or the repository agent-plan wrapper, never raw Viewer recommendations and never decision-status beads. Owner decisions close only from explicit owner answers and must update the smallest routed Canon page when they establish durable behavior. Optional P2 migration automation, resource limits, model-based testing, and ambient-adapter refactoring do not block the mandatory epic unless the owner explicitly promotes them.

comments.author: codex
comments.text: Constitutional decomposition record (2026-08-13): AVAILABLE effects are removal of forbidden legacy authority, exact one-way file/section synchronization, configured verification, scoped Git delivery, durable run accounting, causally bounded post-pass repair, setup/docs/quality/release work needed to ship Omnirepo itself, and tests proving those effects. UNAVAILABLE and intentionally absent effects are general repository orchestration, destination-to-source learning, semantic editing inside the sync engine, inference overriding present repository policy, agent repair without current-run causation, and destination deployment/dependency/release/secret/unrelated maintenance. The dependency graph follows durable artifact flow so later effects cannot manufacture missing authority. This serves Managed means authoritative; Precedence is declared, never guessed; The fleet advances despite stragglers; Humans and agents operate the same system.

Replace ad hoc path joining in every authority-bearing adapter with the shared root/relative-path interface, preserving read/write distinctions.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: One secure sync writer is insufficient if config discovery, Git, logs, or agents can escape by another route.
acceptance_criteria: All filesystem/process working directories and mutation targets require typed roots; production searches find no direct unsafe join/write/open at authority boundaries; error context names the owning root.
notes: Feature beads still own their semantic behavior.

title: Add cross-platform containment and race regression matrix
description:
Exercise traversal, aliases, case/Unicode equivalence, roots and leaf links, reparse/junction/mount/hard-link/special objects, concurrent swaps, nested fleet roots, and unsupported filesystem behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Tension Pair 1 makes outside-fleet mutation an absolute failure, so negative tests must be exhaustive on supported platforms.
acceptance_criteria: No fixture observes an effect outside its declared root; rejected repository operations still yield outcomes while peers can continue; capability-specific cases are explicit.
notes: Use deterministic barriers, not sleeps.

title: Build a hermetic fleet lifecycle integration-test harness
description:
Build reusable schema-neutral hermetic fixture primitives for every test workstream: isolated HOME, PATH, environment, network, credentials and Git configuration; temporary source and destination repositories plus bare remotes; deterministic clock, identifiers, signals and process trees; named filesystem, journal and remote fault points; PTY and non-TTY capture; and two-process barriers. This workstream owns fixture mechanics and their self-tests only. It must not own product journey cases, the test evidence schema, final acceptance traceability, or hostile scenario assertions; those are delegated to .74 and .46.

## Acceptance Criteria

Harness self-tests prove deterministic reusable fixtures, fixed-seed replay, explicit barriers and no wall-clock sleeps or ambient services. Named APIs cover partial and failed writes, sync/replace failure, run-ID collision, accepted-but-disconnected push, executable replacement, post-exit descendants, and intervening worktree edits. Specialized suites compose these primitives without copying mechanisms. Fixture failures identify the primitive and preserve artifacts; unsupported platform capability is explicit, never silently green. The harness has no product authority path and cannot make an E2E case pass by bypassing the public binary.
design: This issue is an outcome container, not the preferred unit of execution. Its child leaves decompose discovery/design, implementation, negative/failure handling, integration, and proof so work can be reviewed and landed incrementally. External parent blockers remain authoritative; leaf tasks add the narrow prerequisite edges needed for safe parallel work. When every child is closed, a human or agent reopens this container, verifies the original description and structured acceptance criteria against combined evidence, records any residual gap as a new child, and closes the container only when no gap remains.
acceptance_criteria: Harness self-tests prove deterministic reusable fixtures, fixed-seed replay, explicit barriers and no wall-clock sleeps or ambient services; named APIs cover partial and failed writes, sync/replace failure, run-ID collision, accepted-but-disconnected push, executable replacement, post-exit descendants and intervening worktree edits; every specialized suite can compose these primitives without copying mechanisms.
notes: Low-level hermetic fixture owner. .74 owns test orchestration, structured evidence, replay bundles, and executable journeys; .46 owns hostile scenario assertions; .48/.49/.62 own platform, scale, and optional model views. Do not grow this into a second test runner.

title: Define deterministic lifecycle fault points and fixture interfaces
description:
Specify named boundaries for config load, source snapshot, plan, journal, lease, file transaction, verification process, agent attempt, commit, push, summary, cancellation, and crash injection.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Later lifecycle tests need reproducible failures without sleeps or ambient services.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned fault-point table names before/after semantics, observable evidence, and expected cleanup; fixture APIs are mechanism-neutral.
notes: Do not encode undecided policy outcomes in the harness.

title: Build isolated filesystem, HOME, clock, identity, and path fixtures
description:
Provide per-test HOME/config/source/destination/run-record roots, fake clock and run IDs, supported path aliases, dirty Git states, permissions, links, special files, and deterministic cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Hermetic state prevents tests from touching the developer fleet or relying on host defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cannot escape their temp root; parallel tests are independent; clock/ID collisions and filesystem races are barrier-controlled; unsupported capabilities skip explicitly.
notes: No real user configuration is read.

title: Build controllable process, network, Git, and agent doubles
description:
Provide fake executables and local endpoints for hangs, forks, signals, oversized/chunked output, auth, HTTP status, Git remote acceptance ambiguity, agent protocol violations, and late writes.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Subprocess and remote effects must be testable without invoking real agents or publishing externally.
acceptance_criteria: Each double exposes deterministic barriers and evidence; no wall-clock sleeps, external internet, ambient credentials, real push, or installed agent dependency is required.
notes: All children are reaped.

title: Add crash, restart, concurrent-process, and persistence controls
description:
Allow tests to terminate the parent at named durable boundaries, launch independent Omnirepo processes, corrupt/truncate journals, simulate ENOSPC and writer failure, and restart against retained fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Crash recovery cannot be proven by in-process errors alone.
acceptance_criteria: Tests can reproduce PID reuse, stale lease, concurrent runs, partial journal tail, post-commit crash, post-remote-acceptance disconnect, and cleanup races deterministically.
notes: Keep policy expectations in consuming tests.

title: Publish harness usage patterns and anti-flake rules
description:
Document how consumers compose the low-level hermetic fixture layer: fixture selection, named fault points, barrier protocol, seed/replay identity, platform capability checks, and prohibition on sleeps or retries as synchronization. This bead owns harness usage guidance and anti-flake rules at the primitive layer; composed-suite stress belongs to .74.9 and final journeys to .74.7.

## Acceptance Criteria

Examples cover one component, one process tree, one crash/restart, and one concurrent fleet case using the .9 primitives; lint or review checks reject wall-clock sleeps in lifecycle tests; every example names the fixture owner and evidence bundle path.
design: A shared harness becomes harmful if each test invents its own timing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Examples cover one component, one process tree, one crash/restart, and one concurrent fleet case; lint or review checks reject wall-clock sleeps in lifecycle tests.
notes: Primitive-layer usage documentation. Do not duplicate .74 runner or journey documentation.

title: Self-test the hermetic fixture layer
description:
Self-test only the reusable .9 fixture primitives: isolated HOME/PATH/environment, fake clock and identity, filesystem and Git roots, process/network doubles, barriers, signals, fault injection, PTY capture, and cleanup ownership. This is not the product acceptance suite and does not rerun every fleet journey. It proves that the lower-level fixtures are deterministic and safe for consumers such as .74, .46, .39, .70, and .42.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each fixture primitive has an isolated self-test with fixed-seed replay, explicit barrier control, no wall-clock sleep, no ambient service, and failure-preserving cleanup. The tests detect leaked descendants, real HOME/network/credential access, cross-case filesystem/Git state, nondeterministic IDs, and missing fault delivery. Consumer suites can depend on these primitives without reimplementing them. Product behavior and final journey coverage remain owned elsewhere.
design: The test infrastructure is part of the trust base and must demonstrate its own failure behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated and parallel runs yield equivalent evidence; escaped effects fail; leaked processes are detected; temporary roots are cleaned or intentionally retained only for diagnostics.
notes: Fixture-layer self-test only. .74.9 owns suite-level isolation and anti-flake stress over composed tests; do not duplicate its journey matrix.
